description: We’re a team of five curious high school students and one Teaching Assistant from Hanoi, taking on our first NASA Space Apps Challenge. We love turning real NASA data into simple, beautiful products that tell a story people remember. Our team covers research, data, coding, design, and we’re ready to build something that connects space to life on Earth.
summary:
LUNAMARIS: Letters Across the Silent Seas is a bilingual (Vietnamese/English) storytelling website for students that works on phones and computers. It answers the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten" by giving four real NASA machines a voice: Apollo 11's laser retroreflector, Surveyor 3, the Opportunity rover and the Ingenuity helicopter. Each one "writes a letter" home to a ground station in Hanoi. To open a letter, players complete a short game built on real mission data. They time a laser pulse's round trip to the Moon, bury Opportunity's solar panels in dust until only 22 Wh remain, or count Ingenuity's flights up to the 72nd. Every number links to a science dossier that cites its NASA source, and the letters are clearly labeled as imagined while the data is labeled as verified. The journey ends with players choosing a landing site for a future Artemis mission. They have to keep it far enough from the old relics to protect them, and they then earn a "Space Heritage Guardian" card.

This matters because most NASA material is in English and full of numbers that are hard to picture. LUNAMARIS turns that data into something students can feel and test for themselves. It also teaches that the hardware we leave behind is heritage worth protecting as we return to the Moon and Mars.
details:
Project Title: LUNAMARIS: Letters Across the Silent Seas

Challenge: Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars
Local Ground Anchor: Hanoi Ground Receiving Station, Vietnam (21.0285° N, 105.8542° E)
Live Demo: lunamaris.vercel.app · Repository: GitHub

What does it do or how does it work?

LUNAMARIS is a high-performance, mobile-first, interactive web application that bridges scientific telemetry with cinematic scrollytelling. Framed as an overnight shift (02:40 AM) at the Hanoi Ground Receiving Station in Vietnam, the user acts as an apprentice alongside mentor Trần Thu Nguyệt when four long-silent signals suddenly chime from across the Solar System:

  1. Dual-Voice Narrative Architecture with Epistemic Labeling: Each chapter cleanly decouples poetic empathy from empirical science through strict cognitive badges:
    • [📡 The Machine's Pulse] (NARRATIVE INTERPRETATION GROUNDED IN TELEMETRY): Poignant first-person postcards sent across the vacuum by the hardware itself.
    • [🏛️ Archaeologist & Science Dossier] (VERIFIED SCIENTIFIC & LEGAL RECORD): Peer-reviewed technical dossiers detailing operating mechanisms, current degradation status, and space preservation statutes.
    • Apollo 11 LRRR (Moon, 1969-059C): Users fire Earth-based laser pulses (2.56 s2.56\text{ s}2.56 s round-trip) and manipulate an observation slider (1969→20261969 \to 20261969→2026) to calculate cumulative lunar orbital recession (Δd=Δt×3.8 cm/yr→+216.6 cm\Delta d = \Delta t \times 3.8\text{ cm/yr} \to +216.6\text{ cm}Δd=Δt×3.8 cm/yr→+216.6 cm in 2026).
    • Surveyor 3 & Apollo 12 (Moon, 1967-035A): Users adjust the landing proximity (2,500 m→50 m2,500\text{ m} \to 50\text{ m}2,500 m→50 m) of LM Intrepid, observing how hypervelocity rocket exhaust (v=300–2,000 m/sv = 300\text{–}2,000\text{ m/s}v=300–2,000 m/s) sandblasts regolith, pitting optical glass and discoloring white paint at the historic 160 m160\text{ m}160 m distance (verified by NASA SP-284).
    • Opportunity Rover MER-B (Mars, 2003-032A): Users increase atmospheric optical depth (τ∈[0.6,10.8]\tau \in [0.6, 10.8]τ∈[0.6,10.8]), watching Martian skies blacken while piecewise JPL telemetry models the plummet of solar power from 645 Wh/sol645\text{ Wh/sol}645 Wh/sol down to its final 22 Wh/sol22\text{ Wh/sol}22 Wh/sol signal on Sol 5111.
    • Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (Mars, 2020-052B): Users fly through Flights 1 to 72 (17.0 km17.0\text{ km}17.0 km, 128.8 min128.8\text{ min}128.8 min, 2,537 RPM2,537\text{ RPM}2,537 RPM), witnessing navigation failure over featureless ripple dunes and its rebirth as a stationary meteorological and avionics testbed logging daily surface data for ∼20 years\sim 20\text{ years}∼20 years.
    • Zone A is eliminated because rocket blast would blind Apollo 11's retroreflectors (violating the ≥2.0 km\ge 2.0\text{ km}≥2.0 km buffer).
    • Zone B is eliminated due to permanent crater shadows that starve solar power (Opportunity's lesson).
    • Zone C is eliminated because featureless, untextured dust disorients optical landing sensors (Ingenuity's lesson).
    • Zone D is approved! As the Artemis astronauts return to Earth, DUSTER is left behind on the lunar surface to monitor the very dust that threatened its predecessors. The user seals the "Fifth Letter" from DUSTER. In the epilogue set in Hanoi in the year 2076 (50 years later), a next-generation night operator receives this exact letter, completing the cycle: "Listen to old machines to know where to take our next steps."

What benefits does it have?

  • Demystifies Complex NASA Science: Translates dense, multi-hundred-page technical reports (e.g., NASA SP-284, Faller 2014, NSSDCA tables) into intuitive, visual, touch-driven mathematical playgrounds.
  • Presents a Plug-and-Play STEM Resource ("15-Minute Teacher’s Corner"): Provides secondary school science and physics educators with structured 5-minute modules spanning optics (d=c⋅t/2d = c \cdot t / 2d=c⋅t/2), atmospheric radiative transfer (τ\tauτ), vacuum projectile mechanics, and space ethics.
  • Raises Awareness of Space Heritage Law: Directs public attention to binding space conservation frameworks, including NASA's 2011 Recommendations to Space-Faring Entities and the One Small Step to Protect Human Heritage in Space Act (U.S. Public Law 116-275 / NASA GIC 21-07).
  • Guarantees Zero-Friction Universal Access: Built with a Zero-CORS, zero-backend architecture. Anyone can run the complete application offline simply by double-clicking index.html in any browser, requiring no Node.js installations, API keys, or cloud servers.

What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Paradigm Shift in Heritage Perception: Shifts the global narrative away from viewing discarded extraterrestrial hardware as "space junk" or "dead scrap," reframing them as humanity’s longest-running extraterrestrial material science laboratories and monuments of shared perseverance.
  • Inspiration for Emerging Space Nations: Anchoring the telemetry receiver in Hanoi, Vietnam illustrates that space science and heritage guardianship belong to the entire global youth, not exclusively to established space powers.
  • Promoting Scientific Rigor & Combating Misinformation: Every figure in the app includes an interactive "Where does this number come from?" drawer citing primary sources, teaching young learners how to verify historical and telemetry data rather than repeating unvetted internet lore.
  • Fostering Early Stewardship for the Artemis Era: As commercial and national missions to the Moon multiply rapidly, Lunamaris prepares tomorrow's engineers and leaders to actively defend historical lunar and Martian landing sites.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Languages & Core Architecture: HTML5 (semantic structure), CSS3 (Tailwind CSS utility styling and custom hardware keyframes), Vanilla JavaScript (modular ES6+ split across app.js, svg-engine.js, story.js, games.js, book.js, decision-station.js, and certificate.js).
    • Pure Interactive Inline SVG paired with CSS transform/filter pipelines for real-time telemetry rendering—deliberately avoiding heavy 3D/WebGL engines to ensure flawless 60 FPS performance across budget smartphones.
    • HTML5 Canvas API for generating custom, downloadable "Space Heritage Guardian" digital badges entirely in client memory.
    • Claude Max (Argon model) & Qoder: Accelerated responsive UI scaffolding, SVG coordinate math, and state routing.
    • Google NotebookLM & Gemini: Synthesized dense NASA mission PDFs and standardized bilingual English/Vietnamese technical terminology.
    • Human Verification Gate: 100% of mathematical formulas, COSPAR IDs (1969-059C, 1967-035A, 2003-032A, 2020-052B), landing coordinates, and legal statutes were manually vetted against original NASA records.

How is your project creative?

  • The Unifying Motif of "Extraterrestrial Dust": Rather than presenting four disconnected trivia cards, Lunamaris weaves a single scientific thread spanning 1967 to 2076:
    • Apollo 11's prisms fear micro-dust blinding;
    • Surveyor 3 was scoured by Apollo 12's engine dust blast;
    • Opportunity fell asleep under a global dust storm;
    • Ingenuity clipped its blade over featureless dust dunes;
    • Artemis IV deploys DUSTER to study and guard against that very same dust!
  • Interactive "Heritage Loop" Storytelling: Users don't merely read about space history—they absorb its scars as engineering constraints to safely land Artemis IV, deploy a real future science payload, pen their own message, and see it echoed back 50 years later in 2076.
  • Cinematic Subtitle Aesthetic: Eschewing cartoonish speech bubbles, Lunamaris employs cinematic typography and dynamic SVG horizon atmospheres (.scene-horizon) that evoke the quiet solitude of an astronomical control center.
  • Gamified Treaty Compliance: International space law and ballistics equations are transformed into tactile game mechanics: players must physically place earned law stamps onto lunar landing maps to reject unsafe landing zones.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Child Safety & Digital Privacy (Zero-PII Compliance): To protect our core target audience (11–15-year-old students) and comply strictly with NASA Space Apps Under-18 rules and COPPA, the application collects zero personal information. Names and nicknames for the Guardian Badge are rendered 100% locally in browser memory via HTML5 Canvas; no tracking cookies, analytics, or remote database records exist.
  • NASA Brand & Trademark Integrity: Strictly adheres to NASA policy by excluding official NASA "Meatball" and "Worm" logos. All graphical insignia are custom-designed vector SVGs.
  • Low-Bandwidth, Mobile-First Accessibility: Optimized for 375 px375\text{ px}375 px viewports with generous ≥44×44 px\ge 44\times 44\text{ px}≥44×44 px touch targets, WCAG AA color contrast, full keyboard navigation (Spacebar / Arrow keys), and explicit support for prefers-reduced-motion. Every interactive slider features fallback preset buttons in case mobile touch dragging is impaired.
  • Epistemic Truth & Academic Honesty: Distinguishes poetic storytelling from historical facts through prominent labeling tags, ensuring young users are never misled into believing historical probes transmitted emotional English text.
  • Offline Classroom Resilience: Guaranteed offline usability so students and teachers in remote regions with unstable internet can download the repository and explore the complete experience seamlessly.
